about: h10-rule-placement-rerun-2026-11: the rule-placement run re-measured on gbrain v0.60.766.0 with GPT-6.2 Sol, on Claude Code (CLI and Agent SDK), Codex, Hermes, OpenClaw and QM; the instruction-followed endpoints and the report's extra figures (spend, intervals, cost per turn, the original run's counts).

cmd:
import os, subprocess, sys
run, src, where, *cmd = sys.argv[1:]
tmp, name = os.path.split(run)
orig = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(src), '2026-11-07-h10-instruction-placement')
def link(target, path):
    if not os.path.lexists(path):
        os.symlink(target, path)
fake = os.path.join(tmp, 'root', 'docs', 'benchmarks')
os.makedirs(fake, exist_ok=True)
link(run, os.path.join(fake, name))
link(orig, os.path.join(fake, '2026-11-07-h10-instruction-placement'))
sys.exit(subprocess.call(cmd, cwd=os.path.join(tmp, 'root') if where == 'fake-root' else None))
steps.note: The script reads the original run's committed instruction-followed-h10.json by a fixed path, so this builds a folder tree whose docs/benchmarks/ points at the scratch copy and at the original run's committed folder (read only), then runs the script there.

not_rebuilt.reason: It is a text search over each shard's full trial folders, including harness state, workspaces and raw harness logs; those files stayed off the repository (they hold per-trial gbrain tokens), so the search has nothing to run on. They are in the private raw archive.
A one-line filter printed them while reading each shard's own results folder before the merge; those per-shard folders are not committed, only the merged results/ is.
Its one line names the output folder's path on the run machine; the counts it prints are in instruction-followed-h10.json, which is rebuilt.

not_rebuilt.what: The startup rules file size captures
not_rebuilt.reason: They are keyless captures from running the harness images against a fake model endpoint in Docker; verify runs no Docker.
